title: Obi embed token claims
description: The claim set a platform's server puts in the short-lived JWT it signs at Obi button-click (PLAN 11.1c, ADR-0014). The Obi backend verifier (backend .../server/token_verifier.py) is the security-authoritative side; this schema mirrors it and a drift test keeps them in lockstep. THREE business-claim forms exist side by side and the older ones are never dropped (owner decisions §D.13 keuze 4 / ADR-0020): (1) the LEGACY form — company_id/company_name/integration all-three-or-none, the single integration value read as one filled slot; (2) the STRUCTURED form — company_id plus `context` with the three POS/PMS/Accounting slots, company-ID-only (no company name, §D.13 item 2); (3) the DIRECTED form (substep 9.3.1, ADR-0020 Option A) — source_system + target_system (canonical catalog ids) + business_id (≈ company_id). The directed form is what ROUTES; the legacy and structured forms stay accepted for back-compat but no longer drive routing. A note with none of the three forms scopes to obi-general-test only.

iss.description: Issuer — must match a trusted platform issuer in knowledge-base/config/platforms.json.

sub.description: Stable per-user subject. Only a hash of it is ever traced; the raw value is never persisted or logged.

exp.description: Expiry (epoch seconds). exp - iat must not exceed the platform's configured lifetime_minutes.

company_id.description: Opaque customer id. In the structured form (`context` present) it is the ONLY company identity — company-ID-only, no company name (§D.13 item 2). Never a scope axis by itself.

company_name.description: Human-readable customer name. Display/audit only. Legacy form only — the structured form never adds it, but a legacy token still carrying it stays valid.

integration.description: LEGACY single-integration claim, accepted forever (§D.13 keuze 4 — never dropped): read as a token with ONE filled slot. The value resolves through the product catalog (knowledge-base/config/product_catalog.json, canonical id or alias) and fills the slot matching the product's role (e.g. "mews" → PMS filled, POS and Accounting empty). New notes send `context` instead.

source_system.description: DIRECTED form (substep 9.3.1, ADR-0020 Option A): the canonical catalog id of the connection's SOURCE system (e.g. "toast"). Present together with target_system + business_id. Direction is primary — source → target is not the same connection as target → source. The gate resolves it through the product catalog; an unknown system is a 400 before any search. This is the routing claim; `integration`/`context` stay accepted but no longer route.

target_system.description: DIRECTED form (substep 9.3.1, ADR-0020 Option A): the canonical catalog id of the connection's TARGET system (e.g. "mews"). Accounting is a first-class target (D5). Resolved and vend-checked at the gate exactly like source_system; an unknown value is a 400 before any search.

business_id.description: DIRECTED form (substep 9.3.1, ADR-0020 Option A): the opaque customer id for this connection (≈ company_id). Becomes the company-isolation axis for the chat; never a scope axis by itself, and never traced raw.

context.description: The structured integration context (§D.13): the customer's three systems, one catalog product per slot or empty. Slot values are canonical ids from knowledge-base/config/product_catalog.json; aliases resolve through the catalog before validation. An unknown value fails closed at the backend gate: 400 before any search (§D.11). Deliberately slots-only at launch — no connection records, property bindings or selected_connection (decision memo §5).

slots.description: The three §D.13 slot roles. null (or an omitted key) means the slot is empty: an empty slot contributes no slot guides and no pairs, and never hides Obi. A FILLED POS or PMS slot outside the launch allowlist (Toast as POS, Mews as PMS) means Obi is not served for that company; a filled Accounting slot never hides Obi (O4, decision round 2).

pos.description: Point of sale — supplied by Data Hub from its backend configuration. One canonical catalog id, or null for empty.

pms.description: Hotel system (PMS) — supplied by Data Hub from its backend configuration. One canonical catalog id, or null for empty.

accounting.description: Accounting system — supplied by Base from its backend configuration. One canonical catalog id, or null for empty.
